security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, documentation links, and screenshot workflow guidance. A medium contextual risk remains because the guide recommends uploading product screenshots and brand assets to third-party image services without privacy safeguards.

remediation.issue: Sensitive asset uploads to image providers
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to redact customer data, avoid confidential unreleased UI, and confirm provider terms before uploading screenshots, brand assets, or reference images.
When asking about image service API keys, state that users should not paste secret values and should use their normal secret store.

content.value_statement: Teams need polished marketing visuals without a full design cycle for every asset. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code plan images, prompts, mockups, and optimization steps.
actual_capabilities: Selects workflows for blog heroes, social graphics, product mockups, banners, and brand assets.
Compares image generation tools such as Gemini, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Midjourney, Recraft, and Stable Diffusion.
Creates structured image prompts with subject, setting, style, lighting, composition, and technical details.
Lists common social, profile, directory, and OG image dimensions for marketing placements.
Recommends web image formats, compression targets, lazy loading, explicit dimensions, and CDN optimization.
limitations: It guides image work but does not generate images without an external model or design tool.
Provider pricing, model names, and API availability can change after the skill content was written.
AI image models may hallucinate product UI, logos, and detailed text.
High-quality outputs still require user-provided brand assets, dimensions, and review.

use_cases.title: Plan a Blog Hero
use_cases.description: Turn a topic into a visual concept, model choice, aspect ratio, prompt, and web optimization plan.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Mockups
use_cases.description: Use real product screenshots, device framing, annotations, and overlays for accurate launch visuals.

use_cases.title: Scale Social Variants
use_cases.description: Adapt one visual direction into platform-specific sizes for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, Facebook, and listing pages.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Image Prompt
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner blog or social image request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image skill to create a prompt for a [placement] about [topic]. Include subject, setting, style, lighting, composition, dimensions, and optimization notes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the Right Image Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Selecting AI generation, editing, design tools, or screenshots
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image skill to recommend the best workflow for [asset type]. Consider brand consistency, required dimensions, text needs, screenshot accuracy, and budget.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Product Mockup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image skill to plan a product mockup for [product or feature]. Recommend screenshot capture, framing, annotations, safe zones, export sizes, and optimization.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Repeatable OG Image System
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the image skill to design a repeatable OG image workflow for [site or content type]. Include templates, dynamic data, required tags, image sizes, and quality checks.

output_examples.input: Need a hero image for a blog post about email deliverability.
output: Recommended approach: AI generation for a one-off blog hero.
Concept: bright signals moving through a clean inbox path to show deliverability.
Size: 1200x630 for both article hero and social preview.
Optimization: export WebP under 200KB with a JPEG fallback.

output_examples.input: Generate an image of our app dashboard.
output: Recommended approach: do not ask AI to invent the dashboard UI.
Capture a real screenshot at high resolution, then place it in a browser or device frame.
Add callouts, labels, and light annotations after capture.

output_examples.input: We need one visual resized for X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Stories, and Facebook.
output: Recommended approach: create one high-resolution concept, then adapt it with a design tool.
Use each platform size and crop manually where needed.
Keep text and logo placement inside safe areas.

best_practices: Define placement, dimensions, brand assets, and image goal before writing prompts.
Use real product screenshots for UI visuals and AI generation for original concepts.
Compress final assets, set explicit dimensions, add alt text, and test previews at real display sizes.
anti_patterns: Generating product UI screenshots with AI when an accurate screenshot is required.
Requesting long paragraphs or complex brand text directly inside generated images.
Publishing large uncompressed images without responsive formats or lazy loading.

faq.question: Does this skill generate images directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides prompt creation, workflow choice, model selection, mockups, and optimization for external image tools.

faq.question: Which tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It references Gemini, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Midjourney, Recraft, Stable Diffusion, Canva, Figma, and optimization tools.

faq.question: Can it help with product screenshots?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends real screenshots, device framing, annotations, and overlays instead of AI-generated fake interfaces.

faq.question: Can it create platform-specific sizes?
faq.answer: Yes. It lists common dimensions for social feeds, profile banners, directory listings, app assets, and OG images.

faq.question: Is it useful for web performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers WebP, AVIF, compression, lazy loading, explicit dimensions, CDNs, and alt text.

faq.question: What information should users provide?
faq.answer: Users should provide placement, dimensions, brand assets, style goals, budget limits, and any privacy constraints.
